qa.reply:
Yes

Committing input encodings and neighbour variants into the corpus before each fix round's red ensures every rule variant is tested red first. Testing plain text, URI forms, JSON escapes, and separator mutations upfront guarantees the test harness exercises the actual shapes encountered in review, catching violations without passing bad or partially-sanitized state. Requiring neighbour variants alongside rule modifications closes escape hatches where a fix for one variant leaves adjacent mutations untested.

CITE: the corpus also holds at least one row for each input encoding the function will meet
